stories.title: How to lose Trump’s trade war: test Canada’s resolve with threats to hockey sticks
bullet_points: Many people would find it difficult to dislike Canadians.
But not Donald Trump, who in a “hold my beer” moment this week demonstrated that he, at least, finds it easy to resent Canadians.
The US president called the country “difficult and unreasonable”, and in a particularly hysterical moment,  threatened to rename a lake , after trade talks collapsed.

stories.title: ‘My children get one childhood.’ Why more Israelis are leaving the country.
bullet_points: According to the author of one study, “Israel is losing Israelis,” most of them young and highly educated.
It’s a sensitive subject for a country founded as a refuge.
The reasons given include the wars, stresses, and acrimonious civil strife.

stories.title: Hundreds of volunteers pull 360-tonne historic Japanese castle back into place by hand
bullet_points: About 1,800 volunteers pulled ropes to move the 360-tonne Hirosaki Castle keep back into position using hikiya, an ancient Japanese moving technique.

stories.title: From patron to partner: Syria’s new relationship with Russia
bullet_points: For many years, Syria’s government relied heavily on support from Russia just to stay in power.
Now, Damascus has a very different relationship with Moscow.

stories.title: South African police arrest two Thai men for allegedly smuggling parrot eggs
bullet_points: Bird eggs intercepted in homemade incubators at Johannesburg airport as officials try to halt wildlife trafficking  South African police have arrested two Thai nationals in separate incidents for allegedly attempting to smuggle endangered parrot eggs out of the country as authorities try to stem the tide of wildlife trafficking.

A 50-year-old Thai national was arrested at OR Tambo international airport in Johannesburg on 20 August, carrying 50 bird eggs in a homemade incubator in a hand-luggage bag, South Africa’s environment ministry said in a  statement .

stories.title: Mpox is back – and in new countries. How can this outbreak be contained?
bullet_points: The public health emergencies in 2022 and 2024 saw the virus reported in 145 countries, but in the new cases children appear particularly affected  A fresh outbreak of mpox  in Guinea Bissau  – the country’s first – means the virus formerly known as monkey pox is back in the headlines.
Since 2022, there have been  almost 190,000 lab-confirmed cases  of mpox reported worldwide in 145 countries.
Before then, outbreaks of mpox tended to be relatively small and in a handful of African countries, where the viral infection was known to be endemic.

stories.title: In Eswatini, learning golf is a fairway to opportunity for young people
bullet_points: In rural Eswatini, golf programs are helping break down the racial and economic barriers that have long kept young people out of the sport.

stories.title: As US applies ‘D-Day’ economic pressures on Iran, the battle shifts to Iraq
bullet_points: A key goal for Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has been disarming Iraq’s militias, including those backed by, and serving, Iran.

stories.title: Helicopter pilot describes what he's seen rescuing people in Nepal
bullet_points: Andy Thapa is a charter and rescue pilot for a Nepali helicopter company.

stories.title: A vintage sports league’s rallying cry: Take me out to the really old ballgame
bullet_points: In the competitive league of vintage base ball – note, two words – the game is played according to rules used in Massachusetts in the 1860s.

stories.title: UK urged to help free British-Egyptian ‘arrested in Cairo over sister’s activism’
bullet_points: Lawyers claim Eman el-Shazly, from Birmingham, was detained in effort to silence her sister, a critic of Sisi regime  The UK Foreign Office has been asked to intervene to secure the release of a British-Egyptian woman who it is claimed has been arrested in Cairo because of her sister’s political activism.
Eman el-Shazly, a 45-year-old based in Birmingham, was arrested on 16 August while visiting Egypt.
Her lawyers say she has been detained in an attempt to silence her sister Mona, a relentless and harsh critic of the Egyptian government on her UK-based YouTube channel.

stories.title: US counters China as Beijing’s ‘shock wave’ hits African economies

aims to offer alternatives and secure critical minerals supply.

stories.title: Venezuelan opposition up in arms over reports US wants big stake in oil and gas
bullet_points: Critics call move to gain long-term access to country’s massive energy reserves  ‘predatory’ and ‘unconstitutional’  Reports that the US is preparing to claim a big stake in Venezuela’s massive energy reserves have sparked an outcry, with critics describing the move as “predatory” and a “rapacious” land grab.

Several media outlets this week reported that the Trump administration – which abducted Venezuela’s authoritarian president, Nicolás Maduro, in January and has steered the South American country ever since – hopes to secure long-term access to its oil and gasfields.
